correctness.rationale: If m=ba+r with 0≤r<b, rounding either m/b or (m+1)/b produces only a or a+1, even at an integral endpoint. Unbiasedness fixes the weight on a+1, so induction proves the law for arbitrary successive reciprocal-integer denominators and order independence of the terminal law. For any nonreciprocal real q, m=⌊1/q⌋ satisfies 0<mq<1<(m+1)q<2. The interval (m/q,(m+1)/q) has length >1 and contains a positive integer k, giving positive intermediate mass at both m and m+1 and positive terminal mass at 0, 1 and 2. This disproves collapse for all k already at two steps, not necessarily at each k. With j=⌊μ⌋, E[(Z-j)(Z-j-1)]≥0 gives the stated variance bound and equality condition; the three-atom witness makes it strict. For q=2/5 and k=6, exact composition gives masses (3,20,2)/25, mean 24/25 and variance 124/625 versus the single-step 24/625. Zero is absorbing, so the tail is min(1,k/b^n); summing it from n=0 gives the claimed expectation, including k=1 and exact powers of b. These are exact fixed-grid results; neither floating-point arithmetic nor arbitrary slopes or initial states are implied. The frozen rational script was inspected but not run; the main checks are analytic.
